record.question: The top of a 21m high tower makes an angle of elevation of 60° with the bottom of an electric pole and an angle of elevation of 30° with the top of the pole. What is the height of the electric pole?
record.explanation: Let the horizontal separation be d and the pole height be h. From the foot of the pole, tan60° = 21/d, so d = 7√3 m. From the top of the pole, tan30° = (21−h)/d, so 21−h = 7. Therefore h = 14 m, assuming vertical structures on the same level ground. Verified solution (unofficial); original printed paper and worked derivation checked on 26 October 2026.
